_meta.indication: LIBTAYO is indicated for the treatment of patients with metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) or locally advanced CSCC who are not candidates for curative surgery or curative radiation.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study R2810-ONC-1540 (a Phase 2 study of REGN2810/cemiplimab in advanced CSCC)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, non-randomized, multicenter study; patients grouped as mCSCC (Group 1) or laCSCC (Group 2) at 3 mg/kg Q2W and mCSCC (Group 3) at 350 mg Q3W
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with metastatic CSCC and patients with locally advanced CSCC who are not candidates for surgery or curative radiation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint of confirmed objective response rate (ORR) by central review
pivotal_trials.n: Study 1540: Group 1 mCSCC N=59, Group 2 laCSCC N=23, Group 3 mCSCC N=49; efficacy assessed in pooled populations (75 metastatic CSCC and 33 locally advanced CSCC)
pivotal_trials.result: Pooled metastatic CSCC (N=75): confirmed centrally-reviewed ORR 47% (95% CI: 35, 59); 5% CR, 41% PR; median DOR not reached. Locally advanced CSCC (N=33): ORR 49% (95% CI: 31, 67); median DOR not reached.

nct_ctgov.title: Study of REGN2810 in Patients With Advanced Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma

key_safety: Serious adverse reactions occurred in 28% of patients (≥2%: cellulitis, sepsis, pneumonia, pneumonitis, urinary tract infection). Most common toxicities (≥20%) were fatigue, rash, and diarrhea. 17% experienced an immune-related adverse reaction (most common >2%: hypothyroidism, pneumonitis, hepatitis).
target_moa: Cemiplimab is a recombinant human IgG4 monoclonal antibody that targets the programmed death-1 receptor (PD-1); binding of PD-1 to its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2 inhibits T-cell activation, and cemiplimab blocks this interaction (PD-1 blocking antibody).

rems.type: The reviewer did not recommend a REMS; safe and effective use addressed via labeling and routine pharmacovigilance.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Division did not obtain the advice of ODAC as no public health issues required public discussion.

summary.text: This NME BLA received Priority review and Breakthrough Therapy Designation. It was granted regular (not accelerated) approval based on a durable, centrally-reviewed objective response rate considered a direct clinical benefit; no advisory committee was convened and no REMS was required.

citations.quote: On September 6, 2017, REGN2810 (cemiplimab) was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the treatment of adults with metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) and with locally advanced and unresectable CSCC based on demonstration of durable objective responses in Study 1423.

In summary, review of the efficacy and safety data in the BLA determined that cemiplimab should receive regular approval for both types of advanced CSCC: patients with metastatic CSCC and patients with locally advanced CSCC who are not candidates for surgery or curative radiation. requirement.text: 3489-1: Submit the clinical trial report for Trial R2810-ONC-1540 (Groups 1, 2 and 3) with the final analysis of ORR and duration of response in advanced CSCC; trial to enroll at least 150 patients including at least 75 with locally advanced CSCC.

citations.quote: 3489-1 Submit the clinical trial report for Trial R2810-ONC-1540 (Groups 1, 2 and 3) that includes the final analysis of objective response rate and duration of response in patients with advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) including patients with metastatic disease and patients with locally advanced CSCC who are not candidates for surgery or radiation. Trial R2810-ONC-1540 will enroll at least 150 patients including at least 75 patients with locally advanced CSCC. All patients will have the opportunity for at least 1.5 years of follow-up following completion of cemiplimab-rwlc treatment to further characterize the durability of responses in both subgroups.
